plan.contextChunk: This figure is a coordinate plane carrying four straight lines, each in a different color with arrowheads on both ends and tagged with a Roman numeral. The horizontal axis is labeled x and numbered from -7 to 7, the vertical axis is labeled y and numbered from -5 to 5, and a light gray unit grid fills the plotting region. Line I is orange and by far the steepest, rising from below the x-axis at the lower left and exiting through the top of the grid just right of the y-axis, where its label sits. Line II is light blue and the shallowest, entering at the left near x equal to -6.5 on the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at 3, and climbing to about x equal to 4, y equal to 5. Line III is teal, crossing the y-axis at -3 and the x-axis near x equal to 1.5 before rising to that same upper right region. Line IV is dark blue and the only line with a negative slope, entering at the upper left, crossing the y-axis at 3, and descending to roughly x equal to 4, y equal to -4.5. Color and numeral identify the lines, leaving steepness and direction as the properties to read off. The plot supports an exercise in pairing four given linear equations with the correct lines.

interactionPlan.concept: The graph of a linear equation is fully defined by its slope (which controls steepness and direction) and its y-intercept (which anchors its vertical position).
elements: x-axis from -7 to 7 with tick marks, numerical labels, and arrowheads
y-axis from -5 to 5 with tick marks, numerical labels, and arrowheads
Light gray unit grid covering the plotting area
Line I: orange, solid, passing through (0, 3) and (-1, 1), labeled 'I' near the top
Line II: light blue, solid, passing through (0, 3) and (3, 4), labeled 'II' near the top right
Line III: teal, solid, passing through (0, -3) and (2, 1), labeled 'III' near the top right
Line IV: dark blue, solid, passing through (0, 3) and (1, 1), labeled 'IV' near the bottom right
Candidate line: dashed black line, controlled by m and b sliders
Rise-over-run triangle markers for each of the four colored lines (revealed on click)

interactions.label: Candidate line slope (m)
interactions.teaches: Changing the slope rotates the line around its y-intercept, determining how steep it is and whether it rises or falls.

interactions.label: Candidate line y-intercept (b)
interactions.teaches: Changing the y-intercept shifts the entire line vertically without altering its steepness or direction.
Clicking a line reveals its geometric rise and run, connecting the equation's slope directly to the visual steepness on the grid.

demo_steps.title: The y-intercept
demo_steps.narration: Notice how Lines I, II, and IV all cross the y-axis at (0, 3). Adjust the candidate line's y-intercept to b = 3 to see it snap to this shared anchor point.

demo_steps.title: Positive vs. Negative Slope
demo_steps.narration: With the intercept at b = 3, change the slope to m = 2 to match the steep, rising Line I. Then set it to m = -2 to match the falling Line IV.

demo_steps.title: Parallel Lines
demo_steps.narration: Keep the slope at m = 2 but drop the intercept to b = -3. The candidate line shifts down to match Line III. Parallel lines share the same slope but cross the y-axis at different places.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A line's equation breaks its visual appearance into two independent controls: 'b' sets a starting vertical position, and 'm' dictates exactly where it goes from there.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Standard 2D coordinate grid with square proportions so slopes render accurately. Draw Lines I, II, III, and IV as solid, distinctly colored lines extending to the edges of the grid, matching the exact coordinates: Line I (m=2, b=3), Line II (m=1/3, b=3), Line III (m=2, b=-3), Line IV (m=-2, b=3). The dashed candidate line should update based on the sliders, starting at y=x. Rise-over-run annotations should be right triangles with dashed legs and labeled side lengths, mapped to integer coordinates on the grid.

authoredContext:
Match each equation of the linear functions with one of the lines in the figure.

A coordinate plane with x and y axes ranging from -7 to 7 and -5 to 5 respectively. Four lines, labeled I (orange), II (light blue), III (teal), and IV (dark blue), are shown. Line I and Line IV intersect at (0, 3). Line III and Line IV intersect at (1.5, 0). Line II and Line III intersect at (4, 5). Lines I, II, and III have positive slopes, while Line IV has a negative slope.
